title: Control plane Terraform module: upgrade sentinels, canary hooks, and chaos-tested health automations
creator: Priya Desai
description: Create and ship enhancements to the private EKS control-plane Terraform module that add upgrade sentinels, automatable canary hooks, and a suite of health automation to enable safe, auditable rolling control-plane upgrades in customer VPCs. Goals: (1) embed preflight and postflight health checks as Terraform-driven resources and null_resource hooks so upgrades fail early, (2) introduce a lightweight 'control-plane sentinel' (k8s Job + Lambda probe) that validates API server readiness, certificate rotation, KMS access, and cloud-controller-manager connectivity before marking an upgrade complete, (3) provide a repeatable canary path for rolling masters with traffic shadowing and emergency rollback trigger points, (4) surface fine-grained telemetry and deterministic runbook links into the Terraform outputs so Console and Ops can automate rollouts and alerts. Non-goals: re-implement cluster lifecycle orchestration (we'll integrate with the existing provisioner operator), change customer network topology, or modify worker node pool strategies beyond creating upgrade-safe annotations. Approach: add Terraform modules and tests under modules/controlplane/upgrade-sentinel with clear inputs for canary percentage, health-timeout thresholds, and synthetic-check configs. Implement the sentinel as an optional module that deploys to a management namespace in the customer's VPC (configurable) and exposes an SSM/Lambda probe for cases where the control plane is not directly reachable from our control plane. Use null_resource triggers and local-exec hooks to create canary manifests and pause the Terraform apply until canary checks complete (with configurable retries). Include an optional chaos-testing harness (kube-perturb integration) for internal use to validate rollbacks and health gates as part of CI. Ensure all new resources are idempotent, tolerate partial failures, and produce structured Terraform outputs for Console + Runbook linking.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module can be added to an existing private EKS blueprint without manual steps
Upgrades using the module pause at preflight and will automatically abort if sentinel checks fail
Canary path deploys one control-plane instance replacement, runs synthetic API and KV cache checks, and either promotes or rolls back within configured thresholds
Module exposes structured outputs: sentinel_endpoint, last_canary_status, telemetry_dashboard_url, runbook_url
CI pipeline runs chaos harness that intentionally perturbs API server network and verifies rollback triggers inside a synthetic test cluster

Add null_resource hooks for canary orchestration and retries

Code review, security review, and release notes
comments: 2025-02-13 — Priya Desai: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Primary ask from Sales: ability to guarantee control-plane upgrades in regulated customers. PM wishlist includes audit events and KMS preflight checks.

2025-02-18 — Liam O'Connor: Spike completed for sentinel probe patterns. Prototype uses a k8s Job + small Go binary that runs: API /healthz, KV cache warm, certificate chain validation, cloud-controller handshake. Posting prototype in GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-eks-sentinels/pull/12

2025-02-22 — SRE (Aisha Khan): Suggested we surface exponential backoff and jitter in the null_resource pause loop and add a hard timeout to avoid stuck applies. Also requested metrics emitted to the 'priv-controlplane' Prometheus namespace.

2025-02-26 — Security (Daniel Wu): Reviewed KMS access pattern, asked to use least-privilege IAM role and ensure no long-lived keys are rendered in outputs. Marked security_review_required=false after confirming flow uses short-lived STS session tokens.

2025-02-28 — Liam O'Connor: Added initial integration test that runs inside CI on a small synthetic cluster. Test reproduces a control-plane upgrade and validates that the sentinel catches a simulated cloud-controller failure and triggers rollback. Test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3456
rollout_plan: 1) Toggle module opt-in flag on staging account. 2) Run Terraform apply with canary=true and canary_percentage=10. 3) Sentinel probes run preflight checks (30m window) and alert on failures. 4) If sentinel passes, proceed with 3 control-plane nodes replaced sequentially with health checks between each. 5) If sentinel fails at any stage, execute automated rollback via provisioner operator and mark Terraform apply as failed. 6) Post-mortem automatically created with diagnostics and links to runbook and PRs.
notes: - Keep sentinel optional (default false) to avoid surprising existing customers. - Avoid storing secrets in Terraform state; use data sources to fetch ephemeral credentials and pass via Kubernetes secrets created at apply time. - Evaluate using AWS EKS managed control plane events vs in-cluster probes for different network isolation profiles. - Coordinate with Console team to consume the module outputs for UX wiring. - Plan a small beta (3 customers) before making the module GA.
